summary: Modern databases and data platforms are rapidly embedding AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need to move data to separate ML systems. By 2026, an estimated 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search (per ACI Infotech), driving a shift where vectors are treated as a native data type integrated into multimodel databases rather than requiring purpose-built vector stores. Leading platforms now bundle in-database LLM inference, embedding generation, semantic/vector search, and managed model hosting to power RAG and generative AI workloads.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, Document AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless SQL and Python functions for LLM tasks (summarize, translate, sentiment, complete), fine-tuning, and agentic workflows. Cortex Search delivers hybrid semantic + keyword retrieval for RAG, and the newly announced Snowflake Postgres unifies the popular database with Snowflake's analytics and AI on a single governed platform.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE/VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY functions, plus Cortex Search as a fully managed hybrid vector + lexical retrieval service.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in hosted LLMs via Cortex (including Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) accessible through SQL/Python; Cortex Analyst and Cortex Agents enable natural-language querying.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions billed per token processed, Cortex Search billed on serving and storage. No separate infrastructure to manage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (in-database model training) + Vertex AI integration + BigQuery vector search
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, and remote Vertex AI/Gemini models) using standard SQL. It supports embedding generation, RAG applications, BigQuery Graph for relationship analysis, and inference against Vertex AI foundation models.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides a VECTOR_SEARCH function with CREATE VECTOR INDEX for approximate nearest neighbor search, plus text, vector, and hybrid search.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING remote model functions, enabling LLM inference directly from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: On-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based (slots) pricing; BigQuery ML has separate per-TB charges for training, and Vertex AI remote model calls incur Vertex AI inference costs.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database LLM/embedding workflows
databases.description: Open-source PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search, while pgai (from Timescale) brings embedding generation and LLM calls into SQL. The VentureBeat research notes PostgreSQL's ascendancy as vectors become a data type integrated into existing multimodel databases rather than a separate store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL — vector search is provided by the pgvector extension (with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes). Core Postgres has no built-in vector type, so this is marked false per the extension-based criterion.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, which enables calling OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and other model providers plus automatic embedding pipelines directly from SQL; otherwise handled in application code.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; costs depend on self-hosting or managed provider (e.g., Timescale, Neon, Supabase). External LLM API calls billed separately by the model provider.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SQL-based inference via Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using familiar SQL by calling out to Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon Comprehend. It is designed for low-latency inference such as sentiment analysis, fraud detection, and personalization directly from Aurora tables.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Vector similarity search on Aurora PostgreSQL requires the third-party pgvector extension; Aurora ML itself does not provide a built-in vector search engine.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models (e.g., for text generation and embeddings) and SageMaker-hosted models through SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/IO pricing; ML inference incurs separate charges from the called service (SageMaker endpoints, Bedrock tokens, or Comprehend requests).

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (CREATE MODEL SQL with Amazon SageMaker and Bedrock LLM integration)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, with SageMaker Autopilot handling model selection under the hood. It supports in-database predictions at scale and generative AI via integration with Amazon Bedrock LLMs.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Redshift ML is focused on predictive model training/inference; native built-in vector similarity search is not a core Redshift ML feature (embedding/vector workflows typically rely on external services or separate stores).
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference and embedding generation invoked from SQL, and with SageMaker for custom and foundation models.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute (RPU/node) and storage pricing apply; model training uses SageMaker resources billed separately, and Bedrock inference is charged per token.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides a full platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including foundation model APIs, agent frameworks, and MLflow-based lifecycle management. Databricks Vector Search offers a managed, serverless vector database integrated with Unity Catalog governance.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed vector database that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables for similarity search.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to hosted LLMs (Llama, DBRX, Anthropic, etc.), plus fine-tuning and agent-building tools integrated with the lakehouse.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving are billed on dedicated DBU/serving rates plus underlying cloud infrastructure.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector indexing and semantic/hybrid search)
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run semantic, hybrid, and RAG queries within the same database, avoiding a separate vector store. It integrates with popular AI frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex) and Atlas's aggregation pipeline.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is built directly into MongoDB Atlas via the $vectorSearch aggregation stage and a dedicated vector index type (HNSW-based approximate nearest neighbor).
databases.llm_integration: No bundled proprietary LLM; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face) for embeddings and generation, commonly through framework connectors.
databases.pricing_notes: Part of MongoDB Atlas cluster pricing; dedicated Search Nodes can be provisioned separately for vector workloads, billed on cluster/compute tiers.
